messages:
incident-bot: P1: multiple container restarts detected on serving cluster us-west-1 for model redwood-14b. Error rate and latency spike observed. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

Sam: Oncall ack. I'm seeing repeated OOMs for pods in deploy `serve-r14b-pool2`. Restart loop ~1m cadence.

Priya: Attaching error excerpt: ```cuda: driver shutting down: cudaErrorUnknown; runtime: failed to allocate 1372656128 bytes: out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
``` Looks like prefill path.

Tom: Metrics: 99.9p prefill token count jumped from 8k -> 150k for a handful of sessions. Prefill_bytes per-request ~1.5GB. Memory fragmentation after repeated long-prefill requests reported by allocator.

Grace: Customer impact check: two customers see chat sessions fail. One (tenant: zephyr-co) on shared pool; one (tenant: beta-retail) on dedicated but was temporarily routed to shared by yesterday's rollout. CS pinged.

Customer Success Bot: Notified zephyr-co and beta-retail at 21:12 PT; both acknowledged errors and requested ETA.

Sam: Quick mitigations I'm proposing: 1) Add gateway soft-reject for prefill tokens > 80k (return 413 payload_too_large with friendly guidance). 2) Enable runtime "prefill_streaming" toggle to do chunked KV allocations. 3) Cordon/evict hot node with repeated OOMs and bring up pre-warmed spares.

Priya: I'll patch gateway config now. Command: ```helm upgrade gateway-prod ./gateway --set prefill.max_tokens=80000 --reuse-values``` Will return 413 and a short message to client.

infra-bot: kube: patch applied gateway-config-hotfix-021, rollout in progress.

Tom: I'm preparing a runtime flag change: `RUNTIME_PREFILL_STREAMING=1` to split inbound prefill into 8k chunks and allocate KV entries incrementally. This avoids one huge contiguous allocation that triggers driver OOM. Deploying to canary set (2 pods).

Grace: Sending customer note: "We've implemented a temporary throttle on very large prompts and are applying a runtime patch to stream large prefill requests to prevent GPU memory exhaustion. We'll follow up with a full RCA."

Sam: Also scheduling immediate tenant routing change: move zephyr-co off shared pool to spare-dedicated-1. Doing manual route update. ```platformctl route set zephyr-co --pool spare-dedicated-1```

infra-bot: route updated for tenant zephyr-co -> spare-dedicated-1. Pods scheduled and warming.

Priya: Gateway prefill guard live at 21:20 PT. Observability: a small number of requests are being rejected with 413, and the restart rate is down ~70%.

Tom: Canary runtime patch accepted and is returning prefill-rejection payloads for huge requests and chunking others. Sample response for large prefill: {"error":"prefill_too_big","hint":"enable streaming or shorten context","retry_after":60}

Sam: Node `gpunode-7b` shows heavy OOMs, cordoning now and draining. ```kubectl cordon gpunode-7b && kubectl drain gpunode-7b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Evictions caused a handful of failovers but overall stabilized.

Tom: Deployed a temporary allocator defensive limit: if single allocation > 60% of device_free, return a controlled error instead of attempting. This prevents kernel-level OOM and process kill. Rolling to production.

Grace: Customer CS: zephyr-co accepted temporary workaround; beta-retail asked for dedicated routing permanently. Noted for account team.

Sam: Observability note: created temporary dashboard showing `prefill.tokens`, `prefill.bytes`, `oom.count`, `container_restart.count` and alert at oom.count > 5 in 5m.

Priya: After the combined mitigation (gateway guard + streaming + node cordon + allocator limit), OOMs dropped to zero and container restarts stopped. Latency back to normal.

Tom: Root cause hypothesis: memory fragmentation in device allocator when handling very large contiguous KV prefill allocations from long-context prompts. A handful of sessions with 100k-200k token prefill caused single-shot allocations that exhausted available contiguous device memory; kernel then killed processes or driver reset. The recent routing change increased exposure by placing some large-context tenants on shared nodes.

Sam: Action items: - Permanent gateway hard/soft quota per-tenant for prefill tokens (Priya) - Make `prefill_streaming` the default and tune chunk size (Tom) - Improve allocator compaction/defragmentation or use chunked allocations at the allocator level (Tom) - Tenant-aware routing policy to keep high-context tenants on dedicated pools (Grace/Platform) - Postmortem + RCA doc and customer-facing detailed RCA (Grace).

Tom: I'll open PRs for allocator chunking and the 60% safety limit. Also adding unit tests simulating repeated large-prefill churn.

Priya: I'll convert the hot helm update to an infra-managed feature flag in the console so we can opt tenants out instead of global change.

Grace: Handoff: Sam -> Priya for night shift at 22:00 PT. Sam will remain available for escalations. TL;DR to leave in thread.

Sam: TL;DR for handoff: P1 due to GPU OOMs from enormous prefill allocations (~1-2GB) from a tiny subset of long-context sessions. Mitigations applied: gateway prefill cap (413), runtime prefill streaming canary, allocator safety limit, cordoned problematic node, tenant reroute. Monitor dashboards and customer tickets.

Priya: Taking handoff. Monitoring in place. Will start postmortem doc and collect logs. Marking incident mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to mitigated. Creating postmortem ticket INC-1799999999 and assigning to Tom/Priya/Grace.

Grace: Notifying account team and scheduling RCA delivery to customers tomorrow.

Sam: Leaving log snippet for postmortem: ```-- pod serve-r14b-2 --
[21:15:03] runtime: prefill_tokens=182341 prefill_bytes=1.6GB
[21:15:03] runtime: attempting single allocation bytes=1.4GB
[21:15:03] cuda: failed to allocate 1400000000 bytes: driver OOM
[21:15:03] kernel: Out of memory: kill process 23421 (serve) score 999
[21:15:47] kubelet: container restart
```

Priya: I'll kick off postmortem and add owners. If anything regresses, ping incident-bot to reopen.
